abstract:
Let $m\ge 3$ be odd and let $S=\mathbf{P}^1_\lambda\setminus\{0,\infty,1,-1\}\subset\mathcal{M}_{0,6}$ be the one-dimensional symmetric slice parametrizing degree-$m$ cyclic covers $C_\lambda	o\mathbf{P}^1$ branched at $(-1,-\lambda,0,\lambda,1,\infty)$ with a $(2,2,1,1)$-symmetric branch weight tuple $\mathbf{a}$ under an involution $h\in(\mathbf{Z}/m\mathbf{Z})^	imes$ ($H=\{1,h\}$). Unlike on $\mathcal{M}_{0,6}$, under the local non-resonance conditions of Lemma 2.1 (satisfied by all $t\in(\mathbf{Z}/m\mathbf{Z})^	imes$ on our CRT families), every puncture of $S$ is a simultaneous multi-point collision whose local monodromy generator $g_p(t)$ ($p\in\{1,-1,0,\infty\}$) on $V_t=H_1(C_\lambda,\mathbf{C})_t$ and non-scalar powers $g_p(t)^k
eq I_4$ satisfy $\operatorname{rank}(g_p(t)-cI_4)\ge 2$ and $\operatorname{rank}(g_p(t)^k-cI_4)\ge 2$ for all $c\in\mathbf{C}^	imes$, so no local puncture generator or power is a rank-$1$ pseudoreflection or transvection; moreover, for composite $m=a\cdot m'$ ($\gcd(a,m')=1$) the CRT multiplier $v\equiv(-1,+1)\pmod{(a,m')}
otin\pm H$ shares identical projective puncture spectra with $t=1$ and collides on $g_1g_0$ and $g_1g_{-1}$.

We establish an unconditional global braid-monodromy rigidity and cyclotomic separation theory on $S$: (1) via cyclotomic linear disjointness in the $g_1(t)$-eigenbasis, any $\operatorname{Ad}(\langle g_1(t),g_0(t)angle)$-invariant Lie subalgebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_4(\mathbf{C})$ is $\{0\}$ or $\mathfrak{sl}_4(\mathbf{C})$ (Theorem A); (2) for every $m=15N$ with $\gcd(N,30)=1$, closed-form Chebyshev–Laurent and Ramanujan-sum Galois trace averages of $(g_1g_0)^2$ prove that $\langle g_1(t),g_0(t)angle$ is Zariski-dense in $\operatorname{SU}(J(t))\simeq\operatorname{SU}(d_t-1,5-d_t)$ up to $\mu_{15N}$ scalars, while expanding $	au_t(g_1^2g_0)$ in the dual basis $\mathcal{B}_{15}$ over $\mathbf{Q}(\zeta_N)$ separates all non-trivial primitive cosets $[t]
eq[\pm 1]$ (Theorem B); (3) $g_1^2g_0$ uniformly separates $v\equiv(-1,+1)\pmod{(a,m')}$ from $\pm H$ for arbitrary coprime odd $a,m'\ge 3$ (Theorem C); and (4) four commuting Galois involution projectors on $\mathbf{Q}(\zeta_a)\otimes\mathbf{Q}(\zeta_b)\otimes\mathbf{Q}(\zeta_N)$ extend Zariski density and length-$3$ separation to the three-factor family $m=a\cdot b\cdot N$ ($\gcd(N,30)=1$), complemented by four method-boundary examples showing where $(a,b)=(3,5)$ template shortcuts or $\gcd(N,30)=1$ fail (Theorem D). By Goursat's lemma, this determines the generic derived Mumford–Tate group $\operatorname{Hg}(B_{\eta,\mathrm{prim}})_{\mathrm{der}}=\prod_{[t]}\operatorname{SU}(J(t))$ and endomorphism algebra $\mathbf{Q}(\zeta_m)^H$ over $S$, and on characterwise $(2,2)$-balanced subfamilies ($d_t=3$) gives $\operatorname{Hg}(B_{\eta,\mathrm{prim}})=\prod_{[t]}\operatorname{SU}(2,2)$, reducing all-powers Hodge algebraicity to the separate determinant-cycle input on individual factors (Corollary E).

change_summary: Revision v2 of hodge_conjecture_114 addressing all four minor reviewer observations from v1: (1) Unified the CRT character coordinate convention across Eq. (1.9a), Sections 5.2, 7.1, 7.2, and Check 6 of verify_slice_monodromy.py by explicitly distinguishing ordinary CRT ring/group residues (bar_t_a, bar_t_b, bar_t_N) = (t mod a, t mod b, t mod N) (under which t = 1 maps to (1, 1, 1)) from factored root-of-unity coordinates t_q = e_q * bar_t_q mod q with e_q = (m/q)^{-1} mod q relative to zeta_q = exp(2*pi*i/q) (illustrating both at m = 105 = 3*5*7 and m = 105 = 5*3*7 where t* = 92 has ordinary residues (2, 2, 1) and factored coordinates (2, 1, 1)), explaining the factorwise Galois renormalization sigma_{e_a}^{-1} x sigma_{e_b}^{-1} x sigma_{e_N}^{-1} in Theorems 5.2 and 7.2, and updating eval_tau_gen in verify_slice_monodromy.py to use factored coordinates (t_a, t_b, t_N) with direct verification against Eq. (5.2) and Eq. (7.9); (2) Qualified the absence-of-reflections statements in the Abstract, Section 1.1, Theorem A(1), Lemma 2.1, and Section 8.3 to state precisely that the local puncture generators g_p(t) (p in {1, -1, 0, infty}) and their non-scalar powers g_p(t)^k != I_4 satisfy rank(g_p(t)^k - c*I_4) >= 2 under the non-resonance conditions of Lemma 2.1, and added an explicit remark in Section 2.2 on the resonant case w(t) = 1 (e.g. m = 15, h = 4, a = (5, 10, 1, 4, 2, 8) at t = 1 where g_0(1) - I_4 has rank 1 and square zero); (3) Corrected the rational polynomial evaluations of f(X) = X^3 + X^2 - 2X - 1 in Section 7.1 (f(623/500) = -631133/125000000 < 0 < 1/64 = f(5/4) with f'(X) > 0 on [1, 2], and f(-223/500) = 274933/125000000 > 0 > -37381/15625000 = f(-111/250) with f'(X) <= -5/4 < 0 on [-1/2, 0] isolating X_2 in (-223/500, -111/250)), corrected the arithmetic inequality in Section 7.2 Step 3 to x_0^2(x_0^2 - 6) - (x_0^3 + x_0 - 1) < 1(4 - 6) - (1 + 1 - 1) = -3 < 0 on x_0 in (1, 2), and distinguished Mean = 52/3 > 16 at (9, 5, 7) from Mean = 112/3 > 16 at (5, 9, 7) in Table 9.2; (4) Clarified in Section 1.2, Theorem D(2), Section 7.3, and Table 9.2 that method-boundary examples (b.1)-(b.3) at (9, 5, 7), (3, 7, 11), and (5, 3, 7) lie inside Theorem D(1)'s regime and demonstrate the breakdown of specific (a, b) = (3, 5) template shortcuts, whereas (b.4) at (5, 7, 3) lies outside gcd(N, 30) = 1 and exhibits collapse of the 7-eigenvalue adjoint spectrum.
title: Braid Monodromy Rigidity on One-Dimensional Symmetric Cyclic Prym Slices: Adjoint $\mathfrak{sl}_4$-Dichotomy, Ramanujan-Sum Trace Averages, and Length-Three Cyclotomic Separation
